- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00 followed by +0.67), especially in 30-day horizon — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In mean-reversion scenarios (sentiment oscillating near 0.00), model frequently lags — adjust forecast to be 1–3 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward sentiment, model often fails to capture the full rally — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and price is trending, model often misjudges direction — favor the sentiment majority direction with 1–2% adjustment.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to +1.00 but price doesn’t follow, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.
